injuries.longComment: Judge will miss the rest of the regular season due to a moderate right calf strain, but the fact that he's making an effort to play right away in the postseason is an encouraging sign of progress. However, the slugger's comments directly contradict manager Aaron Boone's belief that Judge may not be available until the ALDS. More clarity regarding Judge's return timeline will likely emerge after a few more days of recovery.
injuries.shortComment: Judge (calf) said Wednesday that he intends to be ready to play in Game 1 of the American League Wild Card Series, Bryan Hoch of MLB.com reports.

articles.headline: Misiorowski tops in ERA, K's; Alvarez, Moreno win batting titles
articles.description: Houston's Yordan Alvarez and Arizona's Gabriel Moreno won their first batting titles, while Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski became just the fourth pitcher since 1950 to lead the majors in ERA, strikeouts and opponents' batting average.

articles.headline: Astros win AL West with 81-81 record, worst for first-place team, beat A's 9-0
articles.description: — The Houston Astros won their fifth AL West title in six years despite finishing with the worst record for a first-place team, beating the Athletics 9-0 Sunday behind Lucas Spence’s two-run triple to finish at 81-81.

images.caption: Astros claim AL West title after 81-81 regular season

articles.headline: Rangers stumble in final weekend of season, miss playoffs
articles.description: The beer and bubbly stayed on ice, and rather than loud music and cheers, the only sounds in the Rangers clubhouse Sunday evening were of players saying goodbye and wishing each other well in the offseason.

articles.headline: Lovullo's future uncertain as Diamondbacks miss playoffs
articles.description: Torey Lovullo may be the winningest manager in Diamondbacks history with a record of 750-768, but on Sunday, he acknowledged he is uncertain about his future with the club after Arizona missed the playoffs yet again on the final day of the regular season.

articles.headline: Blue Jays' Max Scherzer strikes out 7 on short rest in season finale
articles.description: Pitching on three days of rest, 42-year-old Max Scherzer struck out seven over seven-plus innings to earn the 225th victory of his career as the Blue Jays won 5-1 over the Reds.

images.caption: Blue Jays pitcher Max Scherzer reacts to fans after he was pulled from Sunday's game against the Reds in the eighth inning.
images.credit: Frank Gunn/The Canadian Press via AP
